title: Sacrifice
summary: Sacrifice as giving up a higher value for a lesser one, and why that is not a virtue on this ladder.

lessons.title: What sacrifice names
lessons.objective: Define sacrifice, on this ladder, as giving up a higher value for a lesser one.

exercises.prompt: On this ladder, what does sacrifice name?

choices.text: Giving up a higher value for a lesser one
Giving up a lesser value for a higher one
Any cost you pay to gain something you want
Any feeling of effort or discomfort

feedback.note: The name is reserved for dropping what you rank higher in order to keep or gain what you rank lower.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of the definition to its role.

pairs.left: The value you give up
pairs.right: The higher one

pairs.left: The value you take instead
pairs.right: The lesser one

pairs.left: The name for that trade
pairs.right: Sacrifice

feedback.note: Sacrifice is not just a loss. It is a loss of the higher value in favor of the lesser one.

exercises.prompt: Complete the definition.

feedback.note: The word higher marks what is surrendered. The lesser value is what is accepted in its place.

exercises.prompt: Build the definition in order.

feedback.note: Keep the order: the higher value is given up, and the lesser value is what remains.

exercises.prompt: Which trade fits the definition of sacrifice?

choices.text: Dropping a career you value more to keep a habit you value less
Spending an evening on study you rank above the party
Paying money for a tool you need more than the cash
Resting so you can do better work tomorrow

feedback.note: Only the first trade surrenders the higher value for the lesser one. The others move toward what ranks higher.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to what it describes.

pairs.left: Higher value given up
pairs.right: The loss that makes the act a sacrifice

pairs.left: Lesser value accepted
pairs.right: What is chosen in place of the higher value

pairs.left: A mere cost for a greater gain
pairs.right: Not this unit’s definition of sacrifice

feedback.note: The definition turns on rank. A cost that buys something you value more is a different kind of trade.

exercises.prompt: Finish the contrast inside the definition.

parts.text: You give up the higher value for a

feedback.note: Lesser means lower on your own ranking of values, not merely smaller in size or price.

exercises.prompt: What must be true of the two values for the trade to be a sacrifice?

choices.text: The one given up ranks higher than the one accepted
They must be equal in your judgment
Other people must approve the loss
The act must hurt, whatever the ranks are

feedback.note: Without a higher value surrendered for a lesser one, the definition does not apply.

lessons.title: Not every cost
lessons.objective: Separate a cost paid to gain a higher value from sacrifice as this unit defines it.

exercises.prompt: You skip a snack you care little about so you can finish work you care about more. Is that a sacrifice on this ladder?

choices.text: No. The thing given up ranks lower than the thing gained
Yes. Any skipped pleasure is a sacrifice
Only if someone else notices the skip
Yes, because work always counts as a loss

feedback.note: A cost is not a sacrifice when what you keep or gain ranks higher than what you give up.

exercises.prompt: Match each trade to the label this unit uses.

pairs.left: Give up a lesser value for a higher one
pairs.right: Not a sacrifice

pairs.left: Give up a higher value for a lesser one
pairs.right: Sacrifice

pairs.left: Pay a price you judge worth the gain
pairs.right: A cost, not a sacrifice

feedback.note: The same outward loss can be a cost or a sacrifice. The rank of the values decides which.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast.

parts.text: Paying a cost to gain a higher value is not a

feedback.note: The unit keeps the word sacrifice for the downward trade, not for every price a person pays.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that marks a cost as not a sacrifice.

feedback.note: If the gain ranks higher, the payment is a cost in service of that value, not a sacrifice.

exercises.prompt: Which everyday idea does this unit refuse to treat as sacrifice?

choices.text: Effort spent to reach something you value more
Trading away what you value more for what you value less
Dropping your top value to protect a minor convenience
Surrendering the greater good for a smaller one

feedback.note: Effort toward a higher value is often called a sacrifice in ordinary speech. This ladder does not use the word that way.

exercises.prompt: Match the action to the rank it assumes.

pairs.left: Saving money you need less than the emergency fund
pairs.right: Lesser given up for higher

pairs.left: Spending the emergency fund on a whim you rank lower
pairs.right: Higher given up for lesser

pairs.left: Training because skill matters more than the spare hour
pairs.right: A cost aimed at a higher value

feedback.note: Look at which value is higher in the person’s own ranking before you apply the word sacrifice.

exercises.prompt: Fill the missing rank.

parts.text: Giving up a lesser value for a

feedback.note: The upward trade keeps the higher value. That is the opposite of the definition.

exercises.prompt: Why can two similar losses get different names?

choices.text: Because the values given up and gained may rank differently
Because only large losses count, whatever you value
Because the name depends on how loudly you complain
Because a loss counts only if it lasts a year

feedback.note: The definition is about which value is higher, not about how the loss looks from outside.

lessons.title: Not a virtue
lessons.objective: Explain why giving up a higher value for a lesser one is not a virtue on this ladder.

exercises.prompt: On this ladder, is sacrifice a virtue?

choices.text: No. Giving up a higher value for a lesser one is not a virtue
Yes. The greater the loss, the greater the virtue
Yes, whenever the loss is noticed by others
Yes, but only when both values are equal

feedback.note: A virtue is not made by surrendering what you hold as higher. That surrender is what this unit refuses to praise.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to the judgment this unit makes.

pairs.left: Sacrifice, as defined here
pairs.right: Not a virtue

pairs.left: Giving up the higher for the lesser
pairs.right: The act that is not to be praised

pairs.left: Treating that loss as moral greatness
pairs.right: A mistake this unit rejects

feedback.note: The unit’s second claim is a refusal: that kind of giving up is not a moral virtue.

exercises.prompt: Complete the moral claim.

feedback.note: The definition and the moral claim go together. The downward trade is identified, then denied the status of a virtue.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that withholds praise.

feedback.note: Praise does not attach to the loss of the higher value. That is why the act is not called a virtue.

exercises.prompt: Why does this ladder refuse to call sacrifice a virtue?

choices.text: Because it is the surrender of a higher value for a lesser one
Because virtuous acts must be easy
Because a virtue cannot involve any choice
Because the word itself is too old to use

feedback.note: The reason is the direction of the trade. What is given up matters more, on the person’s ranking, than what is gained.

exercises.prompt: Match the idea people sometimes praise with the correction.

pairs.left: A loss is noble because it is a loss
pairs.right: Rejected. Rank decides, not the mere fact of loss

pairs.left: The bigger sacrifice is the better virtue
pairs.right: Rejected. That trade is not a virtue at all

pairs.left: Keeping the higher value
pairs.right: Not the act this unit calls sacrifice

feedback.note: Size of loss does not turn a downward trade into a virtue. The unit denies that status outright.

exercises.prompt: Fill the reason the act fails as a virtue.

feedback.note: What makes the act fail as a virtue is the same fact that makes it a sacrifice: the higher value is the one abandoned.

exercises.prompt: Which praise does this unit reject?

choices.text: Calling the surrender of a higher value a moral virtue
Naming that surrender a sacrifice
Checking which of two values ranks higher
Admitting that some choices have a cost

feedback.note: The unit keeps the definition and drops the praise. Naming the act is not the same as calling it a virtue.

lessons.title: Rank decides
lessons.objective: Use the rank of two values to decide whether a trade is a sacrifice.

exercises.prompt: You value your honesty more than a small cash gain, and you refuse the cash. What did you do?

choices.text: Kept the higher value. That is not a sacrifice
Sacrificed honesty for the cash
Sacrificed both values equally
Made no choice about values

feedback.note: Refusing the lesser gain protects the higher value. Sacrifice would have been taking the cash and dropping honesty.

exercises.prompt: Match each ranking to the trade that would be a sacrifice.

pairs.left: Health ranks above a dare
pairs.right: Taking the dare and wrecking your health

pairs.left: A friendship ranks above gossip
pairs.right: Spreading the gossip and losing the friend

pairs.left: Your work ranks above a distraction
pairs.right: Dropping the work for the distraction

feedback.note: In each pair, sacrifice is the choice that abandons the value you already rank as higher.

exercises.prompt: Complete the test.

parts.text: before you call the trade a sacrifice.

feedback.note: Rank is the test. Without it, a cost and a sacrifice look the same.

exercises.prompt: Build the rule for judging a trade.

feedback.note: Surrender is the sacrifice when it hits the higher value. The rule is to identify that value first.

exercises.prompt: Two people give up the same afternoon. One ranks the project above the outing. The other ranks the outing above the project, then skips the outing anyway. Who made a sacrifice?

choices.text: The second person, who gave up the higher value
The first person, who worked on the higher value
Both, because both lost an afternoon
Neither, because time cannot be a value

feedback.note: The same hours can be a cost for one person and a sacrifice for another. Their rankings differ.

exercises.prompt: Match the question to the answer it seeks.

pairs.left: Which value is higher?
pairs.right: The one sacrifice would give up

pairs.left: Which value is lesser?
pairs.right: The one sacrifice would accept instead

pairs.left: Did you keep the higher value?
pairs.right: Then the trade was not a sacrifice

feedback.note: Three checks use one scale: higher, lesser, and which of them the choice actually keeps.

exercises.prompt: Finish the decision rule.

parts.text: If you give up the higher value, the trade is a

feedback.note: The rule is direct. Giving up the higher value is what the word sacrifice picks out.

exercises.prompt: What should you not use as the test?

choices.text: How much the choice hurts, apart from which value is higher
Which of the two values you rank as higher
Whether the choice keeps the higher value
Whether the lesser value is what you accept instead

feedback.note: Pain, effort, and the look of a loss do not replace the ranking of the two values.

exercises.prompt: Build the short test.

feedback.note: Naming comes after ranking. Otherwise the word sacrifice is only a comment on discomfort.

lessons.title: The claim together
lessons.objective: State the whole unit: sacrifice is giving up a higher value for a lesser one, and that is not a virtue.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence states the whole unit?

choices.text: Sacrifice is giving up a higher value for a lesser one, and that is not a virtue
Sacrifice is any cost, and every cost is a virtue
Nothing a person gives up can be named at all
Sacrifice is keeping the higher value, and that is not allowed

feedback.note: The unit has two parts that stay together: the definition, and the denial that the act is a virtue.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of the unit to its job.

pairs.left: Giving up a higher value for a lesser one
pairs.right: The definition of sacrifice

pairs.left: That act is not a virtue
pairs.right: The moral claim

pairs.left: A cost paid for a higher value
pairs.right: Outside the definition

pairs.left: Both parts in one statement
pairs.right: The unit held together

feedback.note: Definition, denial, and the excluded case are one lesson when you can say them in a single breath.

exercises.prompt: Complete both halves.

parts.text: Sacrifice gives up a higher value for a lesser one, and it is not a

feedback.note: The blank is the moral half. The first half already states what the act is.

exercises.prompt: Build the full claim.

feedback.note: The because ties the two halves. The act is not a virtue for the reason the definition already names.

exercises.prompt: Someone says every hard choice is a virtuous sacrifice. What does this unit answer?

choices.text: A hard cost for a higher value is not a sacrifice, and a real sacrifice is not a virtue
Yes. Hardship itself is the virtue
No choice can be hard if values are ranked
Every trade of values is a sacrifice, virtuous or not

feedback.note: The answer uses both lessons: do not call every cost a sacrifice, and do not call a sacrifice a virtue.

exercises.prompt: Match the mistake to the correction.

pairs.left: Calling every cost a sacrifice
pairs.right: Check whether the higher value was given up

pairs.left: Praising that giving up as a virtue
pairs.right: This ladder does not treat it as a virtue

pairs.left: Ignoring which value ranks higher
pairs.right: Rank is what makes the definition work

feedback.note: Each mistake drops one piece of the unit. The correction puts that piece back.

exercises.prompt: Fill both key words.

parts.text: value for a lesser one, and you have a sacrifice, not a

feedback.note: Higher marks the value that is lost. Virtue is the status the unit withholds from that loss.

exercises.prompt: Which pair of ideas must you not split apart?

choices.text: The definition of sacrifice and the claim that it is not a virtue
How tired you feel and how long the day was
The cash price and the store receipt
A passing mood and a change in the weather

feedback.note: The summary is one claim with two halves. Either half alone is only part of the unit.

exercises.prompt: Build the closing line.

feedback.note: That short line is the moral half. It still depends on the definition of what a sacrifice is.

exercises.prompt: A person keeps a lesser comfort and drops a value he himself ranks higher, then calls the drop virtuous. What is wrong on this ladder?

choices.text: The drop is a sacrifice, and a sacrifice is not a virtue
Nothing is wrong, because comfort always outranks other values
The only error is using the word sacrifice
Rank does not matter once the person feels proud

feedback.note: Pride in the loss does not change the rank. The higher value was given up for a lesser one, and that is not a virtue.
